name: BEND run guide correction: lxml, h5py and pysam missing from requirements.txt (upstream)
description: The BEND run guide installed from requirements.txt, which until commit 58ad410 lacked three packages the download and embedding scripts import.

attributes.previous_value: Run within the prepared Python 3.10 environment. This downloads data; it is not a small smoke test.
attributes.value: Run within the prepared Python 3.10 environment. From commit 58ad410 requirements.txt includes lxml, h5py and pysam, which earlier revisions lacked. The curl loop replaces python scripts/download_bend.py, which downloads the whole share (7,251,859,341 bytes listed on 2026-11-17). Gene finding reads only the GRCh38 reference and the gene_finding bed and hdf5 files, 3,509,054,493 bytes with the index. The README asks for the data folder structure to be kept, which these paths do.
attributes.rationale: Upstream problem. scripts/download_bend.py at ac6e80c parses the share listing with BeautifulSoup(..., "lxml"), and scripts/precompute_embeddings.py needs h5py and pysam, but requirements.txt at ac6e80c lists none of the three, so the guide's install step left the download failing with bs4.FeatureNotFound. Reported by a third party as BEND issue #53 in April 2024, not by Rewire. Rewire's first correction (rewire-benchmarks#71, 2026-11-17) installed lxml, h5py and pysam explicitly. Commit 58ad410 added all three to requirements.txt, so the install commands are the same as before and the fix is the repin to 58ad410 (claim bend-recipe-corrections-20261119-guide-checkout on steps.0.shell). This explanation now says that requirements.txt covers the three packages from 58ad410. Its new text also describes the gene-finding-only download, which is recorded in claim bend-recipe-corrections-20261119-gene-finding-download on steps.1.shell.
attributes.upstream_response: No maintainer reply on issue #53, which was still open on 2026-11-19. It has two user comments: the reporter added on 2024-04-02, "For running `precompute_embeddings.py` two more packages are missing: h5py and pysam", and another user wrote on 2025-02-14, "I had the same errors". Commit 58ad410 (PR #79, merged 2026-11-18) added h5py, pysam and lxml to requirements.txt, with numpy<2 and setuptools<81; the PR says it "adds dependencies needed by the tested workflow".

name: BEND run guide correction: dead checkpoint links and folder names (upstream, reported by Rewire, fixed)
description: The BEND baseline checkpoints could not be downloaded through the repository's own code until commit 58ad410, and the configuration named folders the share did not have.

attributes.previous_value: This is the README example verbatim; it computes two models and two tasks. Embeddings are stored as Webdataset tar.gz shards; the next step uses the gene-finding subset.
attributes.value: Adapted from the README example, with the task list narrowed to gene_finding because only those inputs are fetched. When pretrained_models/convnet/ or pretrained_models/awd_lstm/ is missing, ConvNetEmbedder and AWDLSTMEmbedder download the checkpoints with wget from ERDA share aNQa0Oz2lY. The resnetlm configuration loads pretrained_models/convnet, which the maintainer confirmed holds the paper's dilated ResNet; the resnetlm folder on the share is empty. To fetch the checkpoints ahead of time, call bend.utils.download.download_model('convnet', destination_dir='./pretrained_models/convnet/') and the same for 'awd_lstm'. With its default destination_dir the function writes the files directly into ./pretrained_models/, where the configuration does not look.
attributes.rationale: Upstream problem, reported by Rewire. At ac6e80c, download_model in bend/utils/download.py fetched from ERDA share dbQM0pgSlM and the README Embedders table linked share eXAmVvbRSW; both returned 403 on 2026-11-17. ConvNetEmbedder and AWDLSTMEmbedder call download_model when pretrained_models/resnetlm/ or pretrained_models/awdlstm/ is missing, and os.system ignored the failed wget, so the guide's precompute step would have failed later, at from_pretrained. The files were in share f6hdp1zTzh, the one scripts/download_bend.py used, under pretrained_models/convnet/ and pretrained_models/awd_lstm/, not the folder names conf/embedding/embed.yaml used. Rewire's first correction (rewire-benchmarks#71, 2026-11-17) fetched the checkpoints with curl from f6hdp1zTzh into the configured folder names. Commit 58ad410 pointed resnetlm at pretrained_models/convnet/ and awdlstm at pretrained_models/awd_lstm/, and made a failed wget raise. Share IDs at ac6e80c, per file: scripts/download_bend.py used f6hdp1zTzh; download_model in bend/utils/download.py used dbQM0pgSlM; the README Embedders table (lines 72-73) linked eXAmVvbRSW; the README data links (lines 18 and 48) already used aNQa0Oz2lY. Commit 58ad410 moved download_bend.py from f6hdp1zTzh, download_model from dbQM0pgSlM and the README model links from eXAmVvbRSW, all to aNQa0Oz2lY. The 2026-11-17 recipe on rewire-benchmarks#71 used f6hdp1zTzh, the download script's share, even though the README already linked aNQa0Oz2lY for data; that choice was Rewire's, not upstream's. With that, the precompute command downloads the checkpoints itself and the curl loop was dropped. HEAD requests on 2026-11-19 returned 200 under https://sid.erda.dk/share_redirect/aNQa0Oz2lY/pretrained_models/ for convnet/config.json, convnet/pytorch_model.bin (79,177,173 bytes) and awd_lstm/pytorch_model.bin (87,174,249 bytes), and 404 for resnetlm/config.json. Field and previous value are steps.2.explanation on the previous guide; the step indices did not change.
attributes.upstream_response: Fixed by the maintainer in PR #79, merged 2026-11-18 as commit 58ad410; issue closed the same day. Maintainer's reply on issue #78, 2026-11-18T16:19:32Z: "Thank you for letting us know and identifying the old share and directory mismatch. The fix should be on main now. However, the pretrained_models/resnetlm directory is still empty. It appears there has been a duplication and naming mismatch at some point and that the (Dilated) ResNet from the paper is actually in the folder pretrained_models/convnet. I apologise for the confusion. I have tested the automatic download as well as the download script and they both appear to work now. Please let me know if you still have issues. Then I will reopen the issue." The maintainer's only comment on PR #79, 2026-11-18T16:17:51Z: "Looks fine but then again I am approving my own PR", followed by a shrug emoji. PR #79 says the full benchmark and GPU execution were not tested.

name: BEND run guide correction: downloaded the whole 7.25 GB share for one task (ours)
description: Rewire's BEND run guide downloaded every BEND task's data to run gene finding, which needs about half of it.

attributes.previous_value:
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install -e .
python scripts/download_bend.py
attributes.value:
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install -e .
S=https://sid.erda.dk/share_redirect/aNQa0Oz2lY
mkdir -p data/genomes data/gene_finding
for f in GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.fai; do
  curl -fL -o "data/genomes/$f" "$S/data/genomes/$f"
done
for f in gene_finding.bed gene_finding.hdf5; do
  curl -fL -o "data/gene_finding/$f" "$S/data/gene_finding/$f"
done
attributes.rationale: Rewire's own error, not an upstream one. The guide ran python scripts/download_bend.py, which fetches the whole ERDA share: 7,251,859,341 bytes in the f6hdp1zTzh listing on 2026-11-17. Gene finding reads only data/genomes/GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa and data/gene_finding/gene_finding.{bed,hdf5} (conf/embedding/embed.yaml lines 106-109). With the .fai index those are 3,509,054,493 bytes, from HEAD requests on share aNQa0Oz2lY on 2026-11-19. GRCh37.no-chr.fa (3,199,905,630 bytes) is read only by chromatin accessibility (line 128). The step keeps its two pip commands and fetches the four files with curl from aNQa0Oz2lY, the share download_bend.py uses at 58ad410. Share IDs at ac6e80c, per file: scripts/download_bend.py used f6hdp1zTzh; download_model in bend/utils/download.py used dbQM0pgSlM; the README Embedders table (lines 72-73) linked eXAmVvbRSW; the README data links (lines 18 and 48) already used aNQa0Oz2lY. Commit 58ad410 moved download_bend.py from f6hdp1zTzh, download_model from dbQM0pgSlM and the README model links from eXAmVvbRSW, all to aNQa0Oz2lY. The 2026-11-17 recipe on rewire-benchmarks#71 used f6hdp1zTzh, the download script's share, even though the README already linked aNQa0Oz2lY for data; that choice was Rewire's, not upstream's. The prerequisites now give about 3.7 GB of disk in total, with the two checkpoints. Not reported upstream: download_bend.py downloading everything is the documented behaviour.

name: BEND run guide correction: precompute step also embedded enhancer annotation (ours)
description: Rewire's BEND run guide copied the README's two-task precompute example, though the guide trains only gene finding and now fetches only its inputs.

attributes.rationale: Rewire's own error, not an upstream one. The guide's precompute step was README.md line 58 verbatim, task=gene_finding,enhancer_annotation, while the guide's last step trains and evaluates gene finding only. With the gene-finding-only download (claim bend-recipe-corrections-20261119-gene-finding-download) the enhancer annotation inputs, data/enhancer_annotation/enhancer_annotation.{bed,hdf5} (conf/embedding/embed.yaml lines 111-115), are not present, so the second task would fail. The step now names task=gene_finding. The model list, resnetlm and awdlstm, is unchanged; at 58ad410 those Hydra keys load pretrained_models/convnet/ and pretrained_models/awd_lstm/. Not reported upstream: the README example is correct for a user who downloads every task.
